event: First solids condense (CAIs)
Gas disk gone; ~30-40 inner embryos begin stirring each other
notes: Theia among them near 1 AU. Inner-system origin per Hopp et al. 2025.

event: Theia and proto-Earth pass and repass; orbits narrow
notes: Last giant impact at 20-70 Myr after CAIs in most simulations. Co-orbital L4/L5 variant is speculative (Belbruno & Gott 2005).

event: Theia enters Earth's Hill sphere (~1.5 million km)
notes: Accelerating from a few km/s.

event: Theia ~4 degrees wide in Earth's sky at 50000 km
Theia crosses the Roche limit (~18500 km)
notes: Too fast to break up. Both bodies bulge.

event: Contact at ~45 degrees and ~9.5 km/s
notes: Theia ~0.13 Earth masses. Canonical geometry (Canup & Asphaug 2001; Denton et al. 2026).

event: Contact zone vaporized; shocks of tens to hundreds of GPa cross both mantles
notes: Energy ~4-10 x 10^31 J. Peak temperatures above 10^4 K (estimate).

event: Theia's mantle smeared into an arm; its core ploughs into Earth's mantle
Debris torqued into orbit; part of Theia returns for a second hit
notes: In the hot-Theia case a 1.5-1.8 lunar-mass body separates intact (Denton et al. 2026).

event: Theia's core merged with Earth's
notes: Explains the Moon's ~1-1.5% core.

event: Earth spins in ~5 hr inside a rock-vapor atmosphere
notes: 2-3 hr in high-angular-momentum models. Photosphere ~2000-2300 K.

event: ~2% of Earth's mass in Theia mantle reaches the lower mantle
notes: Possible origin of the LLVPs (Yuan et al. 2023).

event: ~40% of the Moon's mass clumped outside the Roche limit
notes: Salmon & Canup 2012. Hours if immediate satellite; years to decades if synestia.

event: Moon assembled at 3-6 Earth radii
notes: ~10 degrees across from Earth. Molten. Orbit ~10-15 hr (estimate).

event: Earth-disk system cools and condenses
notes: Volatiles lost by slow leak into 98-99% saturated vapor (Nie & Dauphas 2019).

event: Lunar magma ocean ~80% solid
notes: Olivine and pyroxene sink (Elkins-Tanton et al. 2011).

event: Plagioclase floats; highland crust begins
notes: Final thickness 40-50 km. The Moon's glow fades.

event: Moon recedes past ~10-20 Earth radii
notes: Early tides ~3400x today's. Passes the evection resonance.

event: Magma ocean near-solid; KREEP left between crust and mantle
notes: Rb-Sr anorthosite ages.

event: Tidal remelting resets lunar rock ages (~4.35 Ga)
notes: Nimmo et al. 2024.

event: Annular eclipses begin
notes: Far Moon becomes smaller than near Sun. Roughly 1-2 Gyr ago.

event: Present: Moon at 60 Earth radii; recedes 38.30 mm/yr
notes: Sun/Moon size ratio ~400; distance ratio ~390.

event: Last total solar eclipse
notes: ~600 Myr from now (Vondrak). Range 250 Myr-1.2 Gyr. Meeus puts the very last at ~1.2 Gyr.
